title: Exact descent of tensoring with a fixed K-flat complex
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ its abelian module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use its unbounded derived category $D(R)$ and localization $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and the K-flat derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. For every K-flat complex $A$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], the functors $B\mapsto A\otimes_R B$ and $B\mapsto B\otimes_R A$ preserve all quasi-isomorphisms and descend to exact functors $D(R)\to D(R)$, canonically identified with $QA\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-$ and $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}QA$. Their coherent integer-shift comparisons are the localization of the signed total-complex maps in [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts]. They take cone triangles to distinguished triangles including the connecting map. Shifts preserve K-flatness and flat terms. On the full derived tensor bifunctor, chain maps between flat-term K-flat fixed arguments, and all derived maps obtained by their localization, induce transformations commuting with shifts in the varying argument; both orders of extracting shifts retain the signed compatibility of that leaf. No boundedness or flatness of cohomology is assumed.

proof.text: Use the canonical additive sheaf tensor and the existing direct-sum totalization. Mathlib's bifunctorMapHomotopyCategory constructs the additive tensor on the homotopy category and quotientCompBifunctorMapHomotopyCategoryIso gives its natural comparison to chain-level tensor. CochainTensorUniverses supplies the required totalization and additive instances, so no separate tensor-colimits proof is needed here.

Use the existing generic mapBifunctorMappingCone₁Iso and mapBifunctorMappingCone₂Iso. The source library's BifunctorTriangulated proves that the induced homotopy tensor functors are triangulated for their canonical signed shifts, including the cone projection and connecting arrow; use those instances rather than reconstructing this calculation.

proof.text: For any quasi-isomorphism f, its cone E is acyclic. K-flatness of A makes Tot(E,A) acyclic. Apply the sheaf braiding degreewise to identify the double complex (E,A) with the transpose of (A,E), then totalize and use mapBifunctorFlipIso. This supplies the signed interchange on totals and proves Tot(A,E) acyclic. The two cone isomorphisms and the cone criterion now prove both fixed tensor functors preserve every quasi-isomorphism, without hypotheses on its endpoints.

For any acyclic E, the signed second-variable shift comparison identifies Tot(E,A[n]) with Tot(E,A)[n]. Shift stability of the acyclic homotopy subcategory proves this acyclic. Flatness of terms is reindexed from i to i+n. The same argument makes the resolving property P selected by site tensor descent stable under every integer shift.

Descend the coherent two-variable chain shifts to the homotopy tensor along the quotient, using the source library's commShift₂OfLocalization. Compare its fixed-argument structures with the canonical source-library structures by CommShift.eq_of_natTransCommShift and strict surjectivity on quotient objects. Replace the fixed-argument fields by these equal canonical structures; transport all naturality and mixed-sign laws along the equalities. This preserves both canonical triangulated structures and canonical shift compatibility of the chain-to-homotopy comparison.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor, preceding construction); categories.tex Tags 04VG/04VK, localization and natural-transformation universal properties; more-algebra.tex Tag 0FNH.

proof.text: Let Qh be derived localization. The chain-level quasi-isomorphism result, fullness of the homotopy quotient and its quasi-isomorphism criterion show that each fixed resolving homotopy tensor followed by Qh inverts quasi-isomorphisms. Site tensor descent supplies that L=P.ι⋙Qh is a localization: transfer localization from the equivalence with the localized resolving category along its published natural isomorphism. No new choice of a resolution is used.

Package the existing resolving property, membership proof, localization proof, homotopy tensor, derived tensor and selected comparisons in ResolvingTensorPresentation and TensorPresentation. All fields reduce to the original choices. The ordinary and derived tensors have explicit, proved equality interfaces to their published definitions, preventing repeated unfolding of dependent category constructions. Construct the comparison from the generic homotopy tensor to the selected homotopy tensor by taking the inverse of the selected chain comparison at the underlying representatives; fullness of the homotopy quotient proves naturality. Restrict this comparison to P×P and compose with the selected resolving comparison. Append the inverse currying counit to compare to the uncurrying of our curried derived tensor; its components are identities. This gives a natural bifunctor comparison e whose values are exactly representativeIso. The selected tensor presentation has an explicit type and is locally protected from unfolding. The private tensorPresentationComparison definition packages the displayed composite once, and tensorPresentation_comparison_app proves its component formula; both are fully constructed from the same selected data.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor and preceding construction); Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 06YT (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side); categories.tex Tag 04VK.

proof.text: Restrict the homotopy tensor in both variables to P and postcompose with Qh. Transport its CommShift₂Int structure to the published derived bifunctor along the localization L in both variables, using e and commShift₂OfLocalization. For each a in P, separately lift its tensor functor through Qh. Extend its resolving comparison through L using liftNatIso, obtaining a comparison normalized to e on every resolving object. Prove this comparison commutes with shifts: the localization-induced fixed shift structure and the full bifunctor's fixed shift structure agree after restriction along L, hence agree by localization uniqueness. Triangulatedness descends along Qh by isTriangulated_of_precomp_iso.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor), two-variable representative descent; more-algebra.tex Tag 0FNH (item-shift-tensor).

proof.text: Compose each normalized homotopy comparison with the canonical quotient-to-derived and chain-to-homotopy comparisons. Whiskering, associators and composition preserve CommShift. The chain comparisons and quotientCompQhIso have identity components. The directly constructed homotopy comparison has, definitionally, the inverse selected chain comparison on representatives. Consequently the resulting chain comparisons are exactly representativeIso on every flat-term K-flat B, in both orders. The full CommShift₂Int supplies naturality on all derived fixed-argument maps and the mixed sign. Finally map_distinguished applied to DerivedCategory.mappingCone_triangle_distinguished gives the two explicit cone-triangle conclusions, including their connecting arrows. This normalization is proved once generically for TensorPresentation before instantiation at the sheaf category, so the final assembly need not repeatedly unfold its dependent comparison types.
